text: {"lessons":["Selling Stock B at a gain felt rewarding, but buying it back at a higher price reminds me to make both decisions from expected returns and portfolio risk, not from the satisfaction of realizing a gain.","Selling Stocks A, C, and E after steep losses may reflect loss aversion and delayed reassessment; I should review each holding objectively and act on current evidence rather than my average cost or discomfort.","My repeated trades and month-to-month account swings are not enough to establish a strategy's success; I should follow a consistent plan, monitor diversification, and avoid reacting to short-term price moves."]}
